leads.summary: Notification cards overlap the inset bar on the top and right edges
leads.consequence: With the shipped 10px gaps_out, a visible 26px top bar in floating mode occupies y=10..36, but a toast begins at y=26+Style.gapsOut(5)=31. The Overlay-layer notification is 5px over the bar at their shared right end; a right bar has the analogous x-axis overlap (28+10 vs 28+5). Until notification clearance includes the actual floating edge inset, a toast covers and intercepts part of the card. The separate open PR #13138 already adjusts this consumer for its competing floating design, but that code is not in the reviewed head.

leads.summary: The rounded corners are still square input hit targets
leads.consequence: When decoration:rounding is positive and bar.floating is true, barSurface paints a rounded Rectangle but Region { item: barSurface } derives a QRegion rectangle from only the item's bounding box. Pointer input at the visually transparent rounded corners hits the bar, rather than the app/desktop visible through them. Add the same radius to the Region, accounting for the animated shownRadius, if those corners are intended to be click-through.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator verified in Quickshell v0.3.1 region.cpp build(): item mask is bounding rect, radius only from Region's own radius; Opus self-check added >=0.3.0 requirement

leads.summary: New floating animations ignore the current base branch's no-animations mode
leads.consequence: The PR introduces two unconditional 379ms NumberAnimations. Current quattro has Style.duration(ms), returning zero when reduceMotion is true, and changed existing bar animations to use it. On VMs the current-base installer turns that mode on by default; toggling window gaps with a floating bar still animates its inset/radius for 379ms despite the no-animations setting. Rebase and wrap both new durations in Style.duration(379).

leads.summary: Two open floating-bar PRs independently implement the same setting and command
leads.consequence: #13140 also adds cmd_floating, a floating bar property, bar.floating config and menu/IPC toggle; #13138 adds a differently computed floating bar based on per-edge margins and explicit theme overrides. Neither is stacked on this PR. A three-way merge of each other head against this head has 5 conflict blocks in Bar.qml, and applying #13140's own diff also rejects both omarchy-bar metadata/usage hunks. Simply retaining both definitions risks the later Bash function overriding the earlier, or a QML duplicate-property error; choosing only one side discards the other's feature. Coordinate implementations and tests before merging either, rather than treating these as additive changes.

leads.summary: Apple Silicon notch-floor PR conflicts at the bar window's size and background
leads.consequence: The two open notch-floor PRs have the same head commit, so this is one competing change, not two independent conflicts. That change replaces the same implicitHeight/color lines changed here; three-way merge of #13641 against this PR has a direct conflict at implicitHeight/color. The two existing source-regex fixtures require incompatible literal implicitHeight forms. Reconcile the host extent, notch floor, card background and test expectations together if either PR merges.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus #13641; coordinator verified #13478 has same head 8249e4f8

leads.summary: An unequal four-sided gaps_out value is reduced to one number before positioning every edge of the floating bar
leads.consequence: Hyprland's shipped Lua gap parser accepts {top,right,bottom,left} as independently chosen numbers, but Style.applyGapsOutJson reads only the first number of its CSS getoption string and floatGap applies that one scalar to the anchored edge and both ends. On a theme or user config with unequal gaps_out sides, the bar no longer lines up with window edges on at least one side. Preserve the four effective components and use the gap for each relevant anchor instead of replicating the first one.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Toasts overlap a floating top/right bar; the first gaps toggle mishandles the inset.

### Toasts overlap the floating bar

`notifications/Service.qml` clears `barSize + Style.gapsOut` (31 px, stock top bar); the floating card reaches `barSize + Style.gapsOut * 2` (36 px). Overlay-layer toasts cover its inner 5 px.

**Suggested change:** Clear `shell.bar.barExtent` when provided, else `barSize` (replacement bars).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 9d878b01)</summary>

# Reproducer: notification toasts overlap a floating top or right bar (reproduced as geometry)

Reviewed head: 9d878b01aa3e27789a9d1269b737fd524efabf06.

Toasts are placed from `shell.bar.barSize + Style.gapsOut` (`shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml`, `liveBarSize` and `barClearance`), which the PR leaves unchanged. A floating bar's card now reaches `Style.gapsOut * 2 + barSize` from its edge (`floatGap` in `Bar.qml`). The toast window is on the Overlay layer, above the bar, so with stock sizes (bar 26 px horizontal and 28 px vertical, `Style.gapsOut` 5 from `gaps_out = 10`) a toast covers the inner 5 px of a floating top bar at its right end, or of a floating right bar at its top. With window gaps toggled off the card is flush again and there is no overlap.

This is a geometric check with the repository's own `NotificationLogic.popupPlacement` and the two formulas above, written in the node style of `test/shell.d/notifications-test.sh`. It is not a screenshot; nothing is rendered.

Run from an Omarchy checkout at the PR head (needs node):

```bash
bash toast-overlap-repro.sh "$PWD"
```

`toast-overlap-repro.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer: with bar.floating, notification toasts start inside a floating
# top or right bar. Uses the repository's own placement helper and the
# clearance formula in notifications/Service.qml.
# Usage: bash toast-overlap-repro.sh <omarchy-checkout>
set -euo pipefail
source "$1/test/shell.d/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')
const notifications = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/notifications/NotificationLogic.js')
const service = fs.readFileSync(root + '/shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml', 'utf8')
const bar = fs.readFileSync(root + '/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml', 'utf8')

// Stock sizes: Style.bar.sizeHorizontal 26, sizeVertical 28, and
// Style.gapsOut 5 (half of Hyprland's default gaps_out 10).
const gapsOut = 5
assert(/floatGap: floating && !windowGapsOff \? \(Style\.gapsOut > 0 \? Style\.gapsOut \* 2 : lastGap\) : 0/.test(bar),
  'a floating bar card sits Style.gapsOut * 2 from its edge')
assert(/liveBarSize: [^\n]*shell\.bar\.barSize\)/.test(service) && /barClearance: liveBarSize \+ Style\.gapsOut/.test(service),
  'toasts clear shell.bar.barSize + Style.gapsOut')

const rows = [['top', 26, 'top'], ['right', 28, 'right']].map(([position, barSize, margin]) => {
  const cardInnerEdge = gapsOut * 2 + barSize
  const toastEdge = notifications.popupPlacement(position, barSize + gapsOut, gapsOut).margins[margin]
  console.log(`# ${position} bar: toast starts ${toastEdge}px from the edge; the floating bar reaches ${cardInnerEdge}px`)
  return { position, cardInnerEdge, toastEdge }
})
for (const row of rows) {
  assert(row.toastEdge >= row.cardInnerEdge, `a toast clears a floating ${row.position} bar`,
    `overlap: ${row.cardInnerEdge - row.toastEdge}px`)
}
JS
```

Actual output at 9d878b01 (exit 1):

```text
ok - a floating bar card sits Style.gapsOut * 2 from its edge
ok - toasts clear shell.bar.barSize + Style.gapsOut
# top bar: toast starts 31px from the edge; the floating bar reaches 36px
# right bar: toast starts 33px from the edge; the floating bar reaches 38px
overlap: 5px
not ok - a toast clears a floating top bar
```

The script stops at the first failed assertion; both rows are printed before it: the top case overlaps by 5 px (31 against 36) and the right case by 5 px (33 against 38).
</details>

### First gaps toggle resizes the bar

Stock `gaps_out = 10` polls as Style's starting value, so `onGapsOutChanged` never assigns the bound `lastGap`. The first toggle pulls it to 0: the window resizes, and on return the card stays flush until Style re-polls. Once set, it also masks a later real `gaps_out` of 0.

**Suggested change:** Assign `lastGap`/`lastRadius` in the existing `Component.onCompleted` instead of binding, and guard `onGapsOutChanged` with `Style.gapsOut > 0 || !root.windowGapsOff`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 9d878b01)</summary>

# Reproducer: the floating bar's window-gaps bookkeeping on stock Omarchy (reproduced)

Reviewed head: 9d878b01aa3e27789a9d1269b737fd524efabf06.

Stock Omarchy ships `gaps_out = 10` (`default/hypr/looknfeel.lua`), which `Style` polls as `gapsOut = 5`. That is also `Style.gapsOut`'s starting value, so no change signal fires at startup and `property int lastGap: Style.gapsOut * 2` stays a live binding. On the first window-gaps toggle, `Style` re-polls 0 and the binding drags `lastGap` to 0: the bar window shrinks to the flush size, and when gaps come back the card stays flush until `Style` re-polls, because `floatGap` falls back to that 0. After one full cycle `onGapsOutChanged` has assigned `lastGap` and later cycles behave as designed. Separately, a `gaps_out` that really is 0 while the shell runs (no toggle flag) keeps the old inset, because every 0 falls back to `lastGap`.

The script copies the PR's floating block out of `shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml` byte for byte (from `property bool floating: false` to the end of the `Connections { target: Style }` block) into a `qmltestrunner` harness with a stub `Style` singleton that has `Style.qml`'s starting values, then steps through the toggle in the order the bar sees it (its own flag probe first, then `Style`'s re-poll). Needs Qt 6 `qmltestrunner` at `/usr/lib/qt6/bin/qmltestrunner`. It does not start the shell or a compositor.

Run from an Omarchy checkout at the PR head:

```bash
bash floating-gaps-repro.sh "$PWD" "$(mktemp -d)"
```

`floating-gaps-repro.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer: the floating bar's lastGap follows Style.gapsOut to 0 on the first
# window-gaps toggle. Copies the PR's floating property block out of Bar.qml
# verbatim into a qmltestrunner harness with a stub Style singleton.
# Usage: bash floating-gaps-repro.sh <omarchy-checkout> <empty-scratch-dir>
set -euo pipefail
src="$1"; work="$2/lastgap"
rm -rf "$work"; mkdir -p "$work/qs/Commons" "$work/tests"

style="$src/shell/Commons/Style.qml"
bar="$src/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml"
start_gaps=$(sed -n 's/^  property int gapsOut: \([0-9][0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$style")
start_radius=$(sed -n 's/^  property int cornerRadius: \([0-9][0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$style")
[[ -n $start_gaps && -n $start_radius ]] || { echo "could not read Style.qml starting values" >&2; exit 2; }

printf 'module qs.Commons\nsingleton Style 1.0 Style.qml\n' >"$work/qs/Commons/qmldir"
cat >"$work/qs/Commons/Style.qml" <<QML
pragma Singleton
import QtQuick
// Stub with the starting values of shell/Commons/Style.qml.
QtObject {
  property int cornerRadius: $start_radius
  property int gapsOut: $start_gaps
}
QML

# Everything from 'property bool floating: false' through the end of the
# 'Connections { target: Style ... }' block, byte for byte.
awk '/^  property bool floating: false$/ { on = 1 }
     on { print }
     on && /^  Connections \{$/ { conn = 1 }
     conn && /^  \}$/ { exit }' "$bar" >"$work/block.txt"
grep -q 'function onGapsOutChanged' "$work/block.txt" || { echo "floating block not found in Bar.qml" >&2; exit 2; }

{
  cat <<'QML'
import QtQuick
import QtTest
import qs.Commons

Item {
  id: harness
  width: 100
  height: 100

  Component {
    id: barComponent

    Item {
      id: root
      // Bar.qml: vertical ? Style.bar.sizeVertical : Style.bar.sizeHorizontal (26 for a top bar)
      property int barSize: 26
QML
  cat "$work/block.txt"
  cat <<QML
    }
  }

  TestCase {
    name: "FloatingBarWindowGaps"

    // Creates the bar the way the shell does: Style still holds its starting
    // values, then its startup hyprctl poll lands.
    function makeBar(polledGapsOut, polledRadius) {
      Style.gapsOut = $start_gaps
      Style.cornerRadius = $start_radius
      var bar = createTemporaryObject(barComponent, harness)
      Style.gapsOut = polledGapsOut
      Style.cornerRadius = polledRadius
      bar.floating = true
      return bar
    }

    // omarchy toggle window-gaps: the bar's own probe sees the flag first,
    // then Style re-polls Hyprland (200 ms later) and reads 0.
    function gapsOff(bar) {
      bar.windowGapsOff = true
      Style.gapsOut = 0
      Style.cornerRadius = 0
    }

    // Stock Omarchy: gaps_out = 10, so Style.gapsOut polls as 5, its starting value.
    function test_stock_windowKeepsFloatingSizeWithGapsOff() {
      var bar = makeBar(5, 0)
      compare(bar.floatGap, 10, "floating gap before the toggle")
      compare(bar.windowExtent, 36, "window extent before the toggle")
      gapsOff(bar)
      compare(bar.floatGap, 0, "gaps off tucks the card")
      compare(bar.windowExtent, 36, "the window keeps its floating size while gaps are off")
    }

    function test_stock_floatsAgainBeforeStyleRepolls() {
      var bar = makeBar(5, 0)
      gapsOff(bar)
      // Toggle back: the probe sees the flag go before Style re-polls.
      bar.windowGapsOff = false
      compare(bar.floatGap, 10, "the card floats again before Style re-polls")
    }

    // After one full off/on cycle the handler has assigned lastGap, so the
    // binding is gone and later cycles behave as designed.
    function test_stock_secondCycle() {
      var bar = makeBar(5, 0)
      gapsOff(bar)
      bar.windowGapsOff = false
      Style.gapsOut = 5
      gapsOff(bar)
      compare(bar.windowExtent, 36, "second cycle: the window keeps its floating size")
      bar.windowGapsOff = false
      compare(bar.floatGap, 10, "second cycle: the card floats again before Style re-polls")
    }

    // A gaps_out that really is 0 (no toggle flag) must not float the card.
    function test_realZeroGapsAtStartup() {
      var bar = makeBar(0, 0)
      compare(bar.floatGap, 0, "gaps_out 0 at startup: no inset")
    }

    function test_realZeroGapsWhileRunning() {
      var bar = makeBar(10, 0)
      Style.gapsOut = 0
      compare(bar.floatGap, 0, "gaps_out set to 0 while running, flag absent: no inset")
    }

    // Control: gaps_out = 20, so Style.gapsOut changes from 5 to 10 at startup.
    function test_gapsOut20() {
      var bar = makeBar(10, 0)
      gapsOff(bar)
      compare(bar.windowExtent, 46, "the window keeps its floating size while gaps are off")
      bar.windowGapsOff = false
      compare(bar.floatGap, 20, "the card floats again before Style re-polls")
    }
  }
}
QML
} >"$work/tests/tst_floating_gaps.qml"

runner=/usr/lib/qt6/bin/qmltestrunner
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software "$runner" -import "$work" -input "$work/tests" -o -,txt
```

Diagnostic check (disposable copy of the extracted block, not a PR change): with `lastGap` and `lastRadius` seeded once in `Component.onCompleted` instead of bound, and `onGapsOutChanged` guarded the way `onCornerRadiusChanged` already is (`if (Style.gapsOut > 0 || !root.windowGapsOff)`), all six cases pass (`Totals: 8 passed, 0 failed`). **Related open PRs**
